title: Kai AML sprint scratchlog - quant + prompt eval
content:
Quick log / playing scratchpad for this sprint. Purpose: try low-bit quant variants with KV caching + small prompt-changing evals; capture rough lat/cost numbers and next steps.

TODAY (3/13) high-level:
- repro baseline: rwlm-30b float16 baseline on g4dn with single-request lat ~420ms (seq len 256, prompt 60, gen 196).
- goal: hit <=300ms p95 while keeping top-1 quality delta <0.5% on dev eval (intent: semantic QA).

EXPERIMENTS RUN (notes, noisy):
1) awq-4bit + kv-cache on prefix reuse (cache warm):
   - config: awq-int4, group-size 128, no remap, KV cache enabled, max_batch 4
   - perf: p50 110ms, p95 260ms (best so far), tokens/sec 380
   - eval micro: EM decrease ~0.9% vs f16 baseline on small qa-set (n=250)
   - odd: occasional token corruption on rare unicode chars (\u2014) -> suspect packing during AWQ packer.
   - notes: file pr to quant-lib with test-case for unicode tokens.

2) gptq-int4 + no kv-cache, batching aggressive (batch=16):
   - config: gptq-4bit, dequantize on-the-fly, batch 16, seq len truncated to 192
   - perf: p50 95ms, p95 480ms (tail hurt by batch scheduling), throughput high but latency bad for single-user SLOs
   - quality: EM drop 1.1%
   - conclusion: good for throughput mode (dedicated), not for hosted-latency tier.

3) nf4 (quant-aware) + kv-cache + small prompt cache TTL experiment:
   - config: nf4 q8-ish pipeline, kv-cache TTL 30s, cache hit ratio on test q-set ~0.43
   - perf: p50 125ms, p95 310ms; cost slightly higher than awq-4bit but more stable
   - quality: EM delta 0.2% - best quality/latency trade so far

PROMPT VARIANTS (for eval harness):
- short-system: "You are a helpful assistant. Answer concisely." + question
- long-chain: add 2-shot examples (avg +70 tokens) -> measure sensitivity to prefix length
- tool-call: structured JSON output enforced -> measure generation compliance rate

NOTES ON KV-CACHE BEHAVIOR:
- observed cache churn when client rotates session-id per request (sigh). Need to add sticky session shim in front of client SDK for experiments.
- cache key granularity: currently session+token-hash. For our reuse pattern (few repeated prefixes) consider prefix-hash only -> will increase hit ratio but risk cross-session leakage.
- experiment: run with prefix-only key on internal eval set, track hit ratio and privacy note.

SHORT TODOS (near-term):
- [ ] Add unicode token repro to quant-lib (PR draft) -> assign to Maya
- [ ] Run full n=2k eval on nf4+kv (CI job RUN-2213) -> schedule overnight
- [ ] Try AWQ remap=on + group-size 64 to see if corruption reduces
- [ ] Add SDK sticky-session shim prototype (quick node proxy)
- [ ] Write up mini-brief for eng-rt sync: perf summary + recommended default profile (nf4+kv for hosted API?)

OPEN QUESTIONS / HUNCHES:
- AWQ artifacts: is corruption due to int8->fp16 path in the runner or during serialization? My hunch: serialization packing loses metadata for >127 token ids.
- TTL semantics: 30s seems ok for interactive web UI but for agent workloads with many short steps maybe lower TTL helps. Need more traces.
- Prompt sensitivity: adding 2-shot examples increases latency (longer prefix) but cache hit improves if same examples reused across requesters. Potential win if we standardize prompt templates across product teams.

SNIPPETS / COMMANDS I RAN:
- python bench/run_microbench.py --model rwlm-30b --quant awq --group 128 --kv-cache --max-batch 4 --seq-len 256
- curl -X POST https://staging.redwood/api/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"prompt":"<prompt>","session_id":"staging-test-1"}'

LOG/SHOUTOUTS:
- Evelyn had a great repro for the Unicode crash on Monday — saved a lot of time.

NEXT STEPS / PLANNING:
- prioritize nf4 pipeline stability and run overnight 2k-eval (Maya/Evelyn/Kai)
- if nf4 holds, propose default hosted profile + canary rollout: 10% traffic nf4+kv for one week
- prepare quick playbook for emergency fallback to f16 if we see >1% quality regression

RANDOM NOTES (brain dump):
- consider small SDK flag: prefer_cache_over_batching = true (for low-latency interactive apps)
- check infra ticket: SRE-1045 about ephemeral node eviction, may explain some bad tails seen during batch=16 runs

-- end scratchlog --
